text: 2 things worth noting : 1) Bad chargers are not too bad, as you show, there are so many protection circuits and the 2 biggest offenders for LiPos would be stopped there - high voltage and too high current. As long as the charger provides 5v, chances are that there's no risk of current over the specs. If it provides more it would be capped by a regulator. The only bad charger that could get through is one with a big ripple voltage (say from 5 to 3.5) and pulsating on that. This would probably get through the protections and slowly hurt the battery, which likes being charged in a Constant Current then Constant Voltage cycle. 2) In event of failure of all the protection circuits and the "battery abuse" getting through, it would *always* blow up the battery, no matter where the failure was (or if all failed at the same time). So "physical location of the fire" is not a good evidence to where the failure was. But good job showing the dangers and demystifying a bit the phone battery. As usual, respecting the LiPo is the best approach.
